claims.text: Bhutan lies high in the Eastern Himalayas between India and China.

findings.quote: Tucked high in the Eastern Himalayas between India and China, Bhutan is one of the world’s most enigmatic destinations
findings.note: The page places Bhutan high in the Eastern Himalayas between India and China.

claims.text: Six Senses Thimphu is in Babesa, Thimphu.

findings.note: The Six Senses Thimphu contact address includes Babesa.
The same address lists Thimphu as the city.

claims.text: The Thimphu, Punakha, Gangtey and Paro lodges sit high on hilltops in the Kingdom's western and central valleys.

findings.quote: Six Senses Thimphu, Six Senses Punakha, Six Senses Gangtey, and Six Senses Paro sit high on hilltops like gemstones throughout the Kingdom’s western and central valleys
findings.note: All four lodges, the hilltop setting and the western and central valleys are stated.

claims.text: Six Senses Bumthang is located near the Chamkar Chhu river, further east.

findings.quote: while Six Senses Bumthang is located near the Chamkar Chhu (river), calling you further east
findings.note: The page puts Bumthang near the Chamkar Chhu river and further east.

claims.text: Accommodation is in villas and suites, including three-bedroom villas.

findings.quote: Six Senses resort in Bhutan offers 82 spacious villas and suites, starting from 645 square feet indoors for the suites and up to 3,681 square feet indoors for the three-bedroom villas.
findings.note: The page lists villas and suites, including three-bedroom villas.

claims.text: Journeys come with a private guide, driver and vehicle.

findings.quote: With a private guide, driver and vehicle, we’ll take you beyond the inspiring scenery and deep into the heart of each valley you explore.
findings.note: Journeys include a private guide, driver and vehicle.

claims.text: Experiences include a sunrise hike to Tiger's Nest and visits to Wangdecholing Palace Museum.

findings.quote: Hike at sunrise to Tiger’s Nest or wander through the history of the mystical Buddhist Kingdom at Wangdecholing Palace Museum.
findings.note: Both the sunrise Tiger's Nest hike and Wangdecholing Palace Museum are listed as experiences.

claims.text: Guests can dine in the Chubjakha Ruin.

findings.quote: Dine in the Chubjakha Ruin and be immersed in feudal Bhutanese times.
findings.note: Dining in the Chubjakha Ruin is offered.

claims.text: Bhutan is described as the world's first carbon-negative country.

findings.quote: As the world’s first carbon negative country, Bhutan is a vibrant tapestry of protected forest and abundant nature
findings.note: The page describes Bhutan as the world's first carbon-negative country.

claims.text: Bhutan has chosen low-volume, high-value tourism.

findings.quote: Bhutan has chosen a path of low-volume, high-value tourism
findings.note: The page matches the claim directly.

claims.text: Four of the lodges, Thimphu, Punakha, Gangtey and Paro, sit high on hilltops in Bhutan's western and central valleys.
